items.title: Norris wins wet São Paulo race as Mercedes seals Constructors’ title
items.summary: FIA Document 81 confirms Norris won the 71-lap wet-dry-wet race in 1:35:23.504, 14.602 seconds ahead of Verstappen; Hadjar completed the podium. Russell spun on the slick-tyre pit exit after moving up to fourth, lost places and recovered to finish fourth; he said he did not know what caused the spin and suggested he may have taken too much risk. The final classification matches Formula1.com. FIA Document 82 records Mercedes on 652 points after Brazil; Formula1.com reports that the team clinched the 2026 Constructors’ title.
items.why_it_matters: Norris converted pole, Verstappen climbed from P21, and Mercedes secured the teams' championship. Russell's pit-exit mistake shaped his race, but he recovered to fourth; the title was sealed regardless.

items.title: Vasseur says tyre temperature was central to Ferrari’s difficult São Paulo weekend
items.summary: Formula1.com reports Leclerc and Hamilton called Ferrari’s performance a disaster, with Leclerc eighth after a five-second penalty and Hamilton ninth. Vasseur said Ferrari struggled to put both intermediate and soft tyres in the right temperature window; he estimated the effect could be around half a second, larger than the tenths gained from upgrades.
items.why_it_matters: Vasseur put tyre-window losses at about half a second and said Ferrari may have pitted Hamilton a little too aggressively for slicks; both are his post-race assessment, not an independent telemetry analysis.

items.title: Final FIA classification applies three five-second penalties
items.summary: FIA Documents 78, 79 and 80 impose five seconds on Oliver Bearman for an unsafe release, Charles Leclerc for contact with Liam Lawson, and Kimi Antonelli for an unsafe release. Formula1.com also reports Leclerc's post-race penalty. Document 81's final order places Lawson seventh, Leclerc eighth, Antonelli fifth and Bearman 17th; its current result table agrees. Document 76 lists lap-time deletions separately, while Document 77 reports the inspected cars complied.
items.why_it_matters: The penalties changed the final order and points; deleted laps and the earlier summons are separate from the three timed sanctions.

items.title: Pirelli records 58 pit stops in wet-to-dry São Paulo race
items.summary: Pirelli says all starters began on Intermediates and every driver used both Intermediates and Softs. Its race graphic records 914 Soft laps (64%) and 521 Intermediate laps (36%), with 45-lap Soft stints for Russell and Leclerc and a 17-lap longest Intermediate stint for five drivers. A separate pit-stop graphic counts 58 stops. McLaren Team Principal Andrea Stella said cooler-than-practice conditions helped the team control tyre temperatures; he said McLaren chose another slick set rather than risk stretching the stint to the finish while rain remained uncertain.
items.why_it_matters: Pirelli's graphics record race outcomes; Stella's explanation of McLaren's tyre-temperature advantage and stop choice is the team's assessment, not an independent telemetry finding.

items.title: Verstappen describes his P21-to-podium drive as a challenging race
items.summary: Formula1.com reports Verstappen started P21, reached second after a strong opening intermediate stint and finished 14.602 seconds behind Norris. He said the car later had a "weird balance"; Hadjar completed a Red Bull double podium in third. On 9 November, Team Principal Laurent Mekies said no simulation predicted the P21-to-P2 recovery, a small Friday issue forced the power-unit penalty, and McLaren were generally faster on race pace. Red Bull still needed to assess how much the balance cost on slicks and Intermediates; Mekies did not identify a race-time mechanical failure.
items.why_it_matters: Mekies' account puts the recovery beyond Red Bull's simulations while crediting McLaren's pace; the source does not establish that Verstappen would have beaten Norris from the front or diagnose a race failure.

sources.label: Formula1.com Laurent Mekies on Verstappen's recovery
